title: Earth, the Sun and the Moon
introduction: Look around. Earth feels like our whole world.
Yet it belongs to a larger space family.
We will meet Earth, the Sun, and the Moon.
We will discover why the Moon shines.

steps.title: Three familiar objects
paragraphs: Earth is the world beneath our feet.
The Sun warms and lights our days.
The Moon often appears in our sky.
They are connected, but they are not the same kind of object.

steps.title: The Sun is a star
paragraphs: The Sun is a star, not a planet.
A star is a huge, very hot ball of gas.
Energy made deep inside the Sun powers its light.
That is why the Sun gives us daylight.
steps.glaux: A star does more than look bright. It makes light.

steps.title: Earth is a planet
paragraphs: A planet is a large, nearly round world moving around a star.
Earth is our home planet.
It has land, oceans, and air.
Earth travels around the Sun.

steps.title: Earth's path around the Sun
paragraphs: Earth moves around the Sun.
This movement is called orbiting.
An orbit is the path one object follows around another.
Earth is one of several planets orbiting our Sun.
The Sun and its orbiting objects form our solar system.
steps.glaux: A path can tell a story without showing its true size.

steps.title: Meet the Moon
paragraphs: The Moon is a natural satellite of Earth.
A satellite travels around another object in space.
Natural means people did not build it.
Our Moon travels around Earth.
It is not a star or a planet.

steps.title: A family with different paths
paragraphs: Earth travels around the Sun.
The Moon travels around Earth.
So, the Moon also journeys through space alongside Earth.
These movements help explain their different names.
steps.glaux: The Moon follows Earth while travelling around Earth.

steps.title: Where sunlight starts
paragraphs: The Sun makes its own light.
That light travels through space.
Light coming from the Sun is called sunlight.
Sunlight reaches Earth and the Moon.

steps.title: Why the Moon shines
paragraphs: The Moon does not make the visible light we see.
Sunlight hits the Moon's rocky surface.
Some light bounces away.
This bouncing is called reflection.
Some reflected light reaches our eyes.
That is why we see a bright Moon.
steps.glaux: The brightest clue is sometimes borrowed light.

steps.title: An everyday clue
paragraphs: Imagine a lamp shining on a pale wall.
The lamp produces light.
The wall looks bright because light bounces from it.
The Sun acts like the lamp.
The Moon acts like the wall.

steps.title: Three objects, one story
paragraphs: Earth is our planet. It orbits the Sun.
The Sun is our star and makes its own light.
The Moon is Earth's natural satellite. It orbits Earth.
Moonlight is sunlight reflected from the Moon's surface.
steps.glaux: Keep this small map of space in your mind.

glossary.definition: A huge, very hot ball of gas that makes its own light.
A large, nearly round world that travels around a star.
The path an object follows around another in space.
glossary.example: Earth follows an orbit around the Sun.

glossary.definition: The Sun and the objects travelling around it.
glossary.example: Earth belongs to our solar system.

glossary.definition: An object, not built by people, that travels around another object in space.
glossary.example: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

glossary.definition: Light that has bounced off something.
glossary.example: The Moon sends reflected light toward Earth.

matching.prompt: Match Earth, Sun, and Moon with planet, star, and natural satellite.
matching.hint: Ask which object makes its own light. Then follow their paths.
matching.right: Yes. Earth is a planet, the Sun is a star, and the Moon is a natural satellite.

earth.star: Stars make their own light. Earth is our planet.
earth.natural satellite: Earth is our planet. The Moon is the natural satellite that orbits it.

sun.planet: The Sun makes its own light. It is a star, not a planet.
sun.natural satellite: The Sun is our star. The Moon is Earth's natural satellite.

moon.star: The Moon reflects sunlight. It does not make the visible light we see.
moon.planet: The Moon travels around Earth. It is Earth's natural satellite.

choice.prompt: Why can we see the Moon shining?
choice.hint: Think about the lamp and wall. Which one makes the light?

options.text: The Moon makes the visible light we see.
options.feedback: The Moon appears bright, but it does not produce this visible light. Follow sunlight from the Sun.

options.text: Sunlight bounces off the Moon and reaches our eyes.
options.feedback: Exactly. The Sun makes light. The Moon reflects some of it toward us.

options.text: The Moon saves sunlight and releases it at night.
options.feedback: It is not stored sunlight. Some light reflects as sunlight hits the Moon's surface.

choice.explanation: The Sun produces sunlight. Some reaches the Moon and reflects toward Earth. Moonlight is that reflected sunlight.
